packageRules.description: Group all Actions bumps (the github-actions manager also covers .forgejo/workflows) into one PR.
Group the Python runtime + dev requirements (base / gpu / convert / dev) into one PR.

NVIDIA CUDA wheels: never cross the pinned major. main.py's Windows DLL preloader hardcodes cublas64_12 / cudnn64_9, so a major bump (cublas 13.x, cudnn 10.x) would silently break GPU inference. The <13 / <10 caps in requirements-gpu.txt already block this; this makes the intent explicit.

Keep workflow actions on floating major tags (@vN). Suppress pin/patch/minor so they are never pinned to an exact patch (upstream moves the @vN tag, so patch fixes land at runtime without a PR — and the local action mirrors only sync tags every 8h, so an exact-patch pin can race the mirror). A new MAJOR still surfaces via the rule below.

crane (mirror-ghcr.yml) is version+hash coupled: CRANE_SHA256 must be updated in the same commit as CRANE_VERSION, and the new release tarball must be uploaded to the instance's 'tools' generic package registry BEFORE the bump lands. Renovate can do neither, so never automerge — surface as a Dependency Dashboard checkbox handled by hand.

Major bumps require manual review — surface as checkboxes on the Dependency Dashboard, do not open the PR automatically, do not auto-merge. Minor/patch still flow through Renovate-side automerge, which waits for both all-ci and its own minimumReleaseAge check (platformAutomerge is off: Forgejo only honours required checks, so it would merge before the release age is met).

yt-dlp chases YouTube's breaking changes — extractor fixes must land within a CI cycle, not after the 3-day release age. Own PR (ungrouped), no minimumReleaseAge, automerge. MUST STAY LAST IN THIS ARRAY: yt-dlp is date-versioned (requirements.txt pins yt-dlp>=2026.x), so the annual year rollover is a pep440 *major* and the blanket major rule above also matches it. Renovate merges every matching rule in array order with later keys winning, so from this position the fast lane survives the rollover; from its old position the January bump would have waited for a Dependency Dashboard checkbox — exactly the stale-extractor state this rule exists to prevent. dependencyDashboardApproval is spelled out for the same reason (last-wins is per property, so omitting it would leave the major rule's approval gate in force).

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Security advisories automerge, MAJOR bumps included: this block is applied on top of packageRules for a vulnerability PR, so automerge:true here deliberately overrides the 'Major bumps require manual review' rule above. The value changed false → true during the GitHub → Forgejo port; keeping it true is a maintainer policy call (a fix only available in the next major should not sit behind a dashboard checkbox), not an oversight — flip it back if security PRs should wait for manual approval like any other major.
